notes: Evidence behind quality_tier placements, NOT an input to the composite. quality_tier is the parameter ordering of the generations we carry; the only maintainer judgment in it is where a model from another family or generation sits, and this file is where such a judgment cites its source (docs/decisions/20260805/1427-quality-tier-is-a-curated-ladder.md). A number here ranks nothing, so rows may carry different benchmarks from one another. Scores whose "source" is empty are recorded but may not back a tier_override.

accepted_sources.name: LiveBench (current table)
accepted_sources.notes: Independent single-harness runs, questions refreshed to resist contamination; results published as an unauthenticated CSV (table_YYYY_MM_DD.csv). Caveat when reading coverage: the roster resets with each question refresh, and open-weight models are what falls off — the 2026-06-25 table is 38 models, 34 of them frontier API models.

accepted_sources.name: SWE-rebench
accepted_sources.notes: Independent runs against GitHub issues collected fresh each window, which is the closest published proxy for the agentic-coding work this product does. Window 2026-05-15..2026-07-01 is 111 problems across 65 repositories; a single window is thin evidence on its own.

swe_rebench_2026_05_15_to_07_01.notes: Highest of any open-weight model in that window; everything above it is a hosted frontier system.

fp8-safetensors.reason: Tops the catalog. Both accepted sources put it ahead of every other model we carry, so the composite's params-and-footprint ordering is not what should decide the top of the ladder here.

nvfp4-safetensors.reason: Same weights as fp8-safetensors, one rung below it because the quantisation is more aggressive. Placement of the pair against the rest of the catalog rests on the same evidence.

livebench_2026_06_25_code_generation.notes: The same table carries a deepseek-v4-flash-0731 row at 76.056 (code_completion 73.913). We ship the base checkpoint, so the base row is the one recorded here.

swe_bench_verified.notes: Recorded only. Kept because it is the number this file was built around before 2026-08-05; deleting it would hide that the placement predates the accepted-source rule.

fp8-safetensors.reason: Sits above the dense and MoE Qwen entries on the strength of an accepted source rather than on total parameter count, which is the case tier_override exists for.

swe_rebench_2026_05_15_to_07_01.notes: Above qwen3.6-35b-a3b (24.7) even though the ladder places the 35B-A3B higher. Recorded rather than acted on — see that model's notes.

qwen3.6-35b-a3b.notes: This model sits above qwen3.6-27b in the ladder (89/90 vs 70/72) while the one accepted source covering both puts it 6.5 points below. Left as it is, deliberately (owner decision, 2026-08-05): one window of 111 problems is thin, LiveBench's current table carries no 35B-A3B so nothing cross-checks it, and the MoE's speed is a real axis quality_tier does not encode — it activates 3.3B of 35B per token against the 27B dense model's 27B. Revisit when a second accepted source covers the pair. The current order is not a measurement either: the composite uses TOTAL parameters by design, which structurally places a MoE above a dense model of similar size.

swe_rebench_2026_05_15_to_07_01.notes: Below its qwen3.6 counterpart (24.7), which is the direction the ladder already has them in.

swe_bench_verified.notes: Recorded only. No accepted source carries this model.
